aspects.says: A compound assignment such as += casts the result back to the left-hand type, so it compiles and wraps where the plain assignment would not compile.
basis: section:A Narrowing Integer Cast Keeps the Low Bits and Never Fails

aspects.says: A conditional expression whose branches are an int and a double has type double, so the int branch is widened too.
basis: section:Widening to float or double Is Implicit and Rounds Large Values
aspects.reason: the compiler decides the expression's type; a test sees only the value a reader's method returns, so no wrong solution here compiles differently from a right one

aspects.says: A cast from floating point clamps values outside the target range to MIN_VALUE or MAX_VALUE instead of keeping low bits.
basis: section:Casting a double to int or long Truncates Toward Zero, Clamps at the Range, and Turns NaN Into 0

aspects.says: Casting a double to an integer type truncates toward zero, so a computed amount just below a whole number loses one; Math.round rounds to nearest, and adding 0.5 before the cast is wrong for negative values.
basis: section:Casting a double to int or long Truncates Toward Zero, Clamps at the Range, and Turns NaN Into 0

aspects.says: String.format without a Locale uses the JVM's default locale, so a number written on one machine may not parse with Double.parseDouble on another; pass Locale.ROOT.
basis: section:Text Conversions: parseInt Rejects Spaces, parseDouble Accepts NaN, and String.format Uses the Default Locale

aspects.says: A cast from NaN gives 0 and Math.round(NaN) is 0, so a value that is not a number becomes a plausible zero unless the code rejects it.
basis: section:Casting a double to int or long Truncates Toward Zero, Clamps at the Range, and Turns NaN Into 0

aspects.says: A narrowing integer cast keeps the low-order bits and never throws, so an out-of-range value becomes another, possibly plausible, number; Math.toIntExact throws instead.
basis: section:A Narrowing Integer Cast Keeps the Low Bits and Never Fails

aspects.says: Double.parseDouble trims spaces and accepts NaN and Infinity, while Integer.parseInt rejects spaces; a parsed double is checked with Double.isFinite.
basis: section:Text Conversions: parseInt Rejects Spaces, parseDouble Accepts NaN, and String.format Uses the Default Locale

aspects.says: A cast between reference types converts nothing: it checks the object's class and throws ClassCastException, so (Long) on an Integer fails.
basis: section:A Wrapper Converts Only to Its Own Primitive: an Integer Is Never a Long

aspects.says: Widening int or long to float, or long to double, needs no cast and rounds values beyond 24 or 53 significant bits.
basis: section:Widening to float or double Is Implicit and Rounds Large Values

aspects.says: An int boxes to Integer, which never equals a Long, so a Map<Long, …> lookup or Set<Long>.contains with an int finds nothing; Number.longValue() reads either wrapper.
basis: section:A Wrapper Converts Only to Its Own Primitive: an Integer Is Never a Long
